title: Character Sheet flow - a description in, a video-reference sheet out (front body HEADLESS)
description:
V1 SCOPE, RE-SCOPED BY FABIO 2026-08-19 - PROMPT ONLY, NO IMAGE INPUT. The user writes the character down and nothing else; the reference-photo path is DEFERRED WHOLE to v2, which kills the one unproven step this card carried (holding identity onto a back view the source photo never shows). Head-swap already covers 'make it look like this person' as a second pass on the finished sheet. Krea2 t2i, Fabio's proven sheet prompt with a [CHARACTER PROMPT] hole, FIXED 8:5 (1280x768 / 1792x1120); user picks 1k or 2k (2k default) and turbo on/off (off default). The headless front body is an OPTIONAL step, ON by default: SAM3 text-selects the head, the mask is grown, Klein 4B inpaints it away with a baked prompt - a method Fabio has run by hand. The other half of the work is the ENHANCER RECIPE: the existing in-graph recipe (the Prompt Enhancement group inside krea2_t2i_template.json) writes a whole SCENE - given 'a 1870s Western Indian Chief' it returns a sun-baked plain, a teepee, dust and a staff in his hand, all of which contradict the sheet - so a character-only recipe replaces it, emitting a noun phrase that drops into the hole. New: a STYLE AXIS, the same skeleton in photoreal / 3D / anime / cartoon by swapping five marked spans. Build = plan.md; prompt payload = prompts.md. The graph is built by STRIPPING krea2_t2i_template.json (raw/ is user-owned - Fabio's bench edit; the exact group-by-group surgery is in plan.md). Everything below is the ORIGINAL brief and still holds, except that a reference photo or an edit model is now v2.

UMBRELLA: MPI-560 - The Flow track (MPI-530 was merged into it 2026-08-16; it was previously the umbrella here). PHASE 4 of the Flow track, and it comes FIRST inside that phase - the sheet is the keystone artifact the swap family consumes. Bench work at the node graph, not app wiring. Members and phase order: tasks/MPI-560/plan.md.

Fabio, 2026-08-09. Three of the four shipped flows are marked for deprecation and only head-swap follows through, so this is the next real flow.

WHAT IT IS. The flow takes EITHER a reference photo OR nothing but a description, and returns a locked character sheet. The user states attributes — who the character is, wardrobe, scars and marks, age, build, hair colour, eye colour, and so on — and the flow RESTRUCTURES that into the prompt shape that produces a sheet, in the layout that is known to work as a VIDEO reference.

THE LORA-TRAINING SHEET IS OUT OF SCOPE — A DIFFERENT BEAST, NOT A LAYOUT OPTION (Fabio, 2026-08-09, correcting this card twice: first it framed the two layouts as a conflict, then as an option; both wrong). His words: a lot of the training sheet is completely different, we are talking about something with 20 different images, it is a whole different beast, but this is something for when the flow is actually addressed, not for now. So tasks/MPI-348/brief.md s8.4 (one square image, face SIDE profile + face FRONT profile + FULL BODY) is a separate and much larger job with a different consumer, addressed when that flow is addressed. THIS card owns the VIDEO-REFERENCE sheet ONLY: three panels, a large 3/4 close-up, full body front, full body back, and the front full body has NO HEAD.

THE VIDEO-REFERENCE SPEC, from Higgsfield's HELL GRIND production brief (95-min AI feature, 15 people, under $500K, 14 days of generation, Cannes Marche du Film 2026), each item with the failure it fixes. (a) THE FRONT FULL-BODY FIGURE HAS NO HEAD — on wide shots the model kept sourcing the face from the tiny blurry full-body figure; remove that head and it has exactly one place to take the face from, the close-up. (b) The portrait panel is a LARGE 3/4 view, never straight-on: 'the sheets the model understands best'. (c) KEEP THE SHEET BORING — neutral grey background, flat light, real skin with visible pores, no retouch, and explicitly NO film grain and NO cinematic lens character baked in, or 'the character will carry that look into every scene and stop reacting to new light'. (d) Always check the pupil CATCH-LIGHT, even on dark eyes: without it the face is dead and no video model can act with it. (e) Pick the most BELIEVABLE candidate face, never the most beautiful — 'a beautiful but fake face will show its fakeness later, in video, when it is too late to fix' — which implies the flow surfaces candidates rather than auto-picking.

TWO INPUT PATHS, THEREFORE TWO MODELS, CHOSEN PER PATH AT THE BENCH. Fabio: it is gonna need two different models anyway — if the user gives a reference we need an EDIT model; if the user does not, we have to look for which model responds better to a prompt that asks it to display the character in that certain way. That is the flexibility with flows: multiple models in one flow, best model per step. The t2i selection question is LAYOUT COMPLIANCE (does the model return the requested panels, in the requested arrangement, with a consistent character across them), NOT aesthetics, and it has no answer on the board yet. THE TWO PATHS ALSO HAVE VERY DIFFERENT RISK. THE PROMPT PATH IS THE EASY ONE AND SHOULD SHIP FIRST: attributes in, no photo, t2i generates an invented character front and back. This is exactly what Higgsfield did (Soul Cinema, prompt to sheet, best of several returns) and it has no identity-projection problem at all. THE REFERENCE-PHOTO PATH IS THE HARD ONE: it must hold identity onto a BACK VIEW the source photo never shows, and nothing on the board proves a local model does that. MPI-348 s7 records Qwen-Edit as strongest at COMBINING images and weak on single-image instruction edits, which is the wrong half; Krea2 is the single-ref identity path (ref_boost ~4, s8.3); Boogu Image Edit is the fallback. Bench that one step alone before building the reference path. If no local path holds a back view, that path ships front + 3/4 close-up only and says so.

TEMPLATE OR ENHANCER — DECIDE BEFORE BUILDING. The user is supplying STRUCTURED fields, and structured fields into a fixed slot template need no LLM at all. An enhancer round-trip (Cubric Prompt) only earns its place if the user types free prose instead of filling a form, or if the wording needs per-target-model shaping. Start with the template; reach for Prompt only when the template measurably falls short.

ONE HIGGSFIELD RULE THAT DOES NOT TRANSFER: their brief says never write an age in any language because 'the content filter becomes much stricter the moment it reads a minor'. That is a hosted-platform filter. Vision runs local models, so age is a normal attribute field here — do not copy that rule across.

THE HEADLESS PANEL IS A MASK OP, NOT A PROMPT. Do not ask a model to draw a headless body. Generate the front body normally, then SAM3-segment the head (docs/masking-sam3.md, sam3.1_multiplex_fp16, click-point or text branch) and remove it, letting the backdrop fill. klein-4b has a real inpaint op and Cubric Prompt's rules already record that Klein's removal path wants the prompt EMPTY. This also honours the brief's hardest asset rule: 'an image never runs through a model twice in full — every extra pass destroys texture and drifts colour; after two passes the face turns symmetrical, plastic and lifeless, and that dead texture later hurts the acting in video.' Their point-change workflow (clothes, scars, blood) is the same shape — edit on the sheet, then composite back through a MASK so the original skin texture survives. head-swap already owns that machinery and MPI-348 s6 already picked the compositing paths.

STRESS TEST IS PART OF THE DEFINITION OF DONE: ten generations, different poses and different light, recognisable 10 out of 10, and tested NEXT TO the other assets and in the light of the scenes ahead — 'a hero who looks stable alone often breaks when he shares the frame with someone. If the test fails, the problem is your description, not the model.'

ADJACENT, SAME BRIEF, SEPARATE CARDS IF WANTED: the LOCATION sheet (3/4 never frontal, one anchor object, one light logic, and the reverse-angle trick found late — generate a VIDEO of the empty location with the camera walking through it, screenshot the angle, texture-clean it: a full location sheet out of a single image, which Vision can already do end to end), and the ASSET REGISTRY (an asset is a PAIR — image plus a descriptor that goes into every prompt word for word; every STATE is its own asset, @roco/@roco_wet/@roco_blood, because mixing states in one text makes the model mix them between shots).

SOURCES: full distillation in ~/.claude/memory/domain/ai-video-asset-production.md. Raw material saved at C:\Users\Fabio\Downloads\seedance_skills\ — 'HELL GRIND project brief (extracted).txt' plus the CINEDANCE, ACTING and LIRA skill files. The recipe/enhancer half of the same brief is Cubric Prompt's MPI-28.
